Database recovered, limits adjusted.

What we're going to do:


• Audit all of our resource priority classes

• Introduce more spare capacity for storage nodes so that we don't have to wait for new nodes to come online

• Revise alerts so it's faster than 5min for us to pinpoint where the failure comes from

**Prometheus autoscaling caused database pod eviction**

A Google managed Prometheus collector autoscaler increased the collectors’ resource requests and restarted collectors across the cluster. The collector pods had a wrongly configured too-high priority, higher than our FoundationDB storage pods.

Kubernetes preempted FoundationDB pods to make room for the collectors. Replacement storage pods then had to wait for new nodes compatible with their storage and compute requirements. This took long enough for FoundationDB to begin data recovery, which extended the outage.

The service recovered and was fully available again after about 20 minutes. We are changing the scheduling and capacity configuration so that monitoring workloads cannot evict database storage pods again.

incidents.name: Thread creation is slow and times out

incident_updates.body:
A bug in undici, the HTTP library bundled with Node.js, prevented new outgoing requests from being dispatched while a long-lived streaming request was open on the same HTTP/2 connection. Under high load, new requests queued behind those streams and timed out. We deployed Node.js 26.5.1, which includes the upstream undici fix.

Thread creation has been stable since the deploy.

We have identified the cause. Thread creation has been stable since the deploy. We are continuing to monitor and will post another update once we are confident the issue is resolved.
